issues.competing_evidence: Thorstensen, Wade & Oke+86 primary abstract gives 0.076351±0.000043 d; Coppejans+16 Appendix A1 uses 0.07637533(13) d as a refined phase ephemeris attributed to private communication.
issues.why_it_matters: The precise ephemeris changes radio orbital phase, while the refined value is not a separately published analysis.
issues.needed_action: For phase-sensitive comparisons, decide whether to use the private-communication ephemeris as a distinct adopted phase clock; retain both values and their provenance.

issues.competing_evidence: Gaia EDR3 geometric posterior 220.14 pc (p16–p84 219.06–221.21) and photogeometric 220.22 pc; older estimates include 260 pc, Thorstensen+03 260(+190/−90) pc or alternate 403(+230/−162), and Urban & Sion+06 270 pc from weak parallax plus other priors.
issues.why_it_matters: Distance choice shifts luminosity and absolute-magnitude comparisons; the legacy estimates combine heterogeneous priors.
issues.needed_action: Use the Gaia geometric posterior for the compatibility field while retaining all literature branches; review if a population analysis requires a non-Gaia distance scale.

issues.competing_evidence: Urban & Sion+06 low-S/N IUE WD+disc fit gives about 28,000 K with adopted Mwd=0.8 Msun and i=41°; its FUV shares are 55/45 and Mdot has order-of-magnitude uncertainty. Knigge+06 gives superhump-sequence estimates M2=0.105±0.023 Msun and R2=0.167±0.012 Rsun; nearby donor-sequence M5/~3100 K is not a SU UMa spectrum.
issues.why_it_matters: Treating fit inputs, a low-S/N composite temperature, or a sequence node as direct component measurements would bias component/population comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Keep model outputs and assumed inputs distinct in the machine-readable ledger; no direct donor type/temperature or dynamical masses are adopted. Confirm this is the preferred presentation for later catalog display.

issues.competing_evidence: Coppejans+16 reports Benz+83 4.75-GHz outburst detection around 1.3 mJy and quiescent <0.4 mJy, but the 2.4-arcmin Effelsberg beam contains a nearby unclassified 33±9 μJy source 0.34 arcmin away. Benz+83 full table was not accessible; details are secondary-reported.
issues.why_it_matters: The historical source association affects whether the system has a long-baseline radio history distinct from the 2015 VLA detections.
issues.needed_action: Keep the 1983 claim flagged as secondary and potentially confused; retrieve the original full article or observing record before using its flux as a secure SU UMa measurement.

issues.competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 4 reports 1–10 and 0.1–10 keV fluxes converted from Collins & Wheatley+10 MEKAL using PIMMS, average characteristic kT=11 keV and unabsorbed flux; no source-specific error, epoch/state or simultaneous radio match is supplied.
issues.why_it_matters: These comparison-band fluxes are not native measurements at the radio epochs and can mislead radio/X-ray correlations if treated as simultaneous or directly fitted values.
issues.needed_action: Keep fluxes labelled as model-dependent conversions and non-simultaneous; do not calculate a matched radio/X-ray ratio without an explicit state/epoch model.
